title: Door control wire shorted
shortDescription: Long flash 1, short flash 1: door control button wire short.
fullDescription:
LiftMaster diagnostic LED beside the Learn button uses long-short patterns. 1-1 (one long, one short) indicates white/red door control wire short to ground.

Disconnect at opener; if LED clears, fault is in wall button or wire.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect wall control
fixSteps.instruction: Remove wall control wires from opener; if LED clears, source is wall side.

faq.q: What is long flash vs short?
faq.a: Long is ~1 second; short is ~0.25 seconds.

title: Wall control button voltage low
shortDescription: 1 long, 2 short flashes: low voltage on wall control circuit.
fullDescription: Code 1-2 means voltage on the wall control wire is below threshold. Often a partial short or moisture in the wall button.

fixSteps.title: Replace wire
fixSteps.instruction: Run new 22-gauge bell wire if needed.

whenToCallPro: If running new wire in walls.

faq.q: Can rain reach my wall button?
faq.a: Some installs have moisture coming from car or roof leaks.

title: Wall control button stuck
shortDescription: 1 long, 3 short flashes: door control button stuck pressed.
fullDescription: If the LED shows 1-3, a button on a wall control or external accessory is stuck pressed. The opener ignores commands while button held.

fixSteps.title: Press button
fixSteps.instruction: Push wall button firmly several times.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: If still stuck, install new wall control.

faq.q: Could a child have stuck a key in?
faq.a: Possible; check button face for obstruction.

title: RPM sensor fault
shortDescription: 2 long, 3 short flashes: motor RPM sensor not detected.
fullDescription:
Code 2-3 indicates the RPM sensor (which detects motor rotation) is faulty or disconnected. The opener cannot determine motion or position.

Usually requires logic board service.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open opener housing, check ribbon cable to RPM sensor.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Contact LiftMaster pro for sensor/board replacement.

title: Door reverses on closing
shortDescription: 3 long, 2 short flashes: close-direction force exceeded.
fullDescription:
Code 3-2 indicates the door reversed during closing because of obstruction or excessive force. Could be debris, ice, broken spring, or force limit set too low.

Manually test door balance and clear obstacles.

fixSteps.title: Clear path
fixSteps.instruction: Remove debris, ice, snow from threshold.

fixSteps.title: Adjust force
fixSteps.instruction: Turn close-force dial slightly clockwise (small increments).

fixSteps.title: Spring check
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect opener; manual lift should be smooth. If heavy, professional spring replacement.

faq.a: Door becomes unsafe; UL325 limits exist.

title: Safety sensor blocked
shortDescription: 4 long, 1 short: safety sensor obstructed or misaligned.
fullDescription: Same as Chamberlain 1-flash: safety beam interrupted. Clean and align sensors.

fixSteps.title: Clean and align
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe lenses, loosen wing nuts, align until receiver LED solid.

title: Safety sensor wire shorted
shortDescription: 4 long, 2 short: safety sensor wire short.
fullDescription: Code 4-2 indicates the white/white-black sensor wire is shorted to ground. Inspect for staples, pinches, and water damage.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sensor leads at opener; if LED clears, fault is in sensor or wire.

title: Limit settings need readjustment
shortDescription: 4 long, 6 short: travel limits not configured properly.
fullDescription:
Code 4-6 means the open and close limits are not set or have drifted. The opener cannot find end-of-travel reliably.

Reprogram limits using the dial buttons on the opener.
symptoms: Door does not fully open or close

fixSteps.title: Reprogram limits
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold opener UP/DOWN buttons per manual to set new open/close positions.

fixSteps.title: Test
fixSteps.instruction: Run door full cycle and confirm it stops correctly.

faq.a: Only after spring change or trolley movement.

title: Logic board failure
shortDescription: 5 long, 5 short: complete logic board fault.
fullDescription:
Code 5-5 indicates a logic board failure beyond simple recovery. After surge events or aged boards, this is common.

Replace the logic board kit (often easier than full opener).

fixSteps.title: Order board kit
fixSteps.instruction: Find OEM LiftMaster logic board for your model number.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power, remove cover, swap board, transfer wire harness, reinstall.

faq.a: Yes; install one on garage circuit.

title: Battery backup needs service
shortDescription: 6 long, 5 short: battery backup error (CA models).
fullDescription:
California requires battery backup on residential garage door openers (SB969). LiftMaster models with backup show 6-5 when the battery is depleted, disconnected, or end-of-life.

Replace the 12V backup battery.

fixSteps.title: Open battery cover
fixSteps.instruction: Side cover on opener houses 12V battery.

fixSteps.title: Replace battery
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM LiftMaster 485LM or compatible 12V SLA.

faq.a: About 1-3 years; CA mandates backup since 2019.

title: LiftMaster LED code 1-1 safety reversing sensor
shortDescription: Safety sensors not aligned or wired.
fullDescription: 1-1 indicates safety sensor wiring fault. Verify white-black to white sensor; white-grey-stripe to grey sensor.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: White and white/grey from each sensor to terminal.

title: LiftMaster LED code 1-3 wall control wiring
fullDescription: 1-3 means wall control wires shorted or wall control failed.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect wall control
fixSteps.instruction: Reset opener with wall control disconnected.

title: LiftMaster LED 1-4 sensor misalignment
shortDescription: Safety sensors not facing each other.
fullDescription: 1-4 = safety sensors misaligned. Adjust until both LEDs solid.

title: LiftMaster LED 1-5 motor RPM sensor
fullDescription: 1-5 indicates motor RPM signal lost. Often connector loose between motor and logic board.

title: LiftMaster LED 2-1 wall control button stuck
fullDescription: 2-1 = wall control reports button held. Check for stuck button or short.

title: LiftMaster LED 4-6 force/limit issue
shortDescription: Door reverses on close due to force or limit.
fullDescription: 4-6 = obstruction or force-set issue during close. Adjust close force/limits and inspect rollers/springs.

fixSteps.title: Adjust close force
fixSteps.instruction: 1/4 turn screw at a time motor head.

title: LiftMaster LED 5-1 motor over-temp
fullDescription: 5-1 = motor over-temperature. Caused by binding door, frequent cycling, or failing motor.

fixSteps.title: Check spring tension
fixSteps.instruction: Manual lift: door should hold mid-travel.

title: LiftMaster LED 3-2 logic board issue
fullDescription: 3-2 = logic board issue, often after surge. Replace board.

title: LiftMaster myQ won't connect
fullDescription: Same root causes as standalone hub: 2.4GHz only, fresh learn press, app current.

title: LiftMaster battery backup replace
shortDescription: Battery backup LED red; backup non-functional.
fullDescription: 475LM battery 5 yr lifespan typical.
